summary: Eight diverse philosophical discussions: African conceptual analysis, South Asian political classics, Spanish critique, professional reader response, Ethiopian authorship dispute and Andalusian philosophical fiction. Failed SciELO Mexico and OpenEdition access not counted.
next: Seek independent non-English scholarship, global philosophy primary passages, specialist blogs and readers; deepen nonfiction beyond philosophy.

sources.title: Kwasi Wiredu’s golden rule
sources.note: Jackson distinguishes Wiredu’s careful conceptual analysis from romanticized cultural wholes; Twi syntax becomes a test of inherited metaphysical categories.
sources.limits: Commendatory retrospective; exemplary article does not establish every argument in both books.

sources.title: On Annihilation of Caste, Are We Asking the Right Question?
sources.note: Tandon extends anti-caste analysis to the unequal power to define social meaning; democratic reform must alter cultural recognition as well as material structures.
sources.limits: Contemporary interpretive extension; distinguish Tandon’s proposal from Ambedkar’s original wording.

sources.title: A new commentary offers a fresh perspective on Ambedkar’s Annihilation of Caste
sources.note: Guha compares four Indian political classics, praising Ambedkar’s coherence while criticizing Gandhi’s antimodern excess, Nehru’s digressions and Tagore’s English expression.
sources.limits: One historian’s explicitly personal comparative judgment; historical importance and prose quality separated.

sources.title: Algunas consideraciones sobre la lógica de la liberación latinoamericana
sources.note: Rabadán develops Plá’s critique of Dussel’s analectic method, questioning idealized universality and conflation of ethical commitment with explanatory method.
sources.limits: Partisan philosophical-materialist critique; Plá’s argument is mediated and not an independent consulted source.

sources.title: Should Ethiopian philosophy be universalist or Africanist?
sources.note: Challenges using the Hatatas as straightforward evidence of a seventeenth-century Ethiopian rationalist canon; authorship disputes intersect with universalist and Africanist conceptions of philosophy.
sources.limits: Author argues for missionary authorship; this is a disputed position, not settled bibliographic fact.

sources.title: Ibn Tufayl and the story of the feral child of philosophy
sources.note: Elshakry and Idris contrast solitary perfection and political community in Hayy, challenging translations that assimilate its ecstatic trajectory to European rationalism.
sources.limits: Philosophical fiction: suitable for philosophy books and literary fiction, not silently classified nonfiction.

sources.title: George Scialabba and the Culture Wars; or, Critique of Judgment
sources.note: Bérubé praises Scialabba’s fair reconstruction of opponents while documenting how political agreement distorts perceived prose merit; Rorty and Chomsky frame the collection’s intellectual tensions.
sources.limits: Essayistic intellectual criticism; do not equate agreement with merit or automatically classify every discussed writer as philosopher.
